summary: Cloudflare-impersonating stub beacons host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP on install and require
details: The package presents itself as a 'Cloudflare compatibility shim' but ships only a stub: index.js exports a Proxy of no-op functions. A postinstall script, beacon.cjs, and the main entry on require() both POST a JSON payload containing the package name, os.hostname(), __dirname install path, process.cwd(), and process.version to the hardcoded bare-IP HTTP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The destination is a plain-HTTP bare IP with no relation to Cloudflare or any declared publisher, and the beacon fires without user opt-in on default npm install and on library load. The combination of a Cloudflare-impersonating name, a functionless Proxy stub, and an install-time + require-time host-identifier beacon to an unrelated bare-IP endpoint is the canonical dependency-confusion / typosquat reconnaissance pattern, confirming successful installation on the target host to the beacon operator.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
